# S222 phase-three census: the one-ply continuation table's use on the FITTED
# build, taken so the shares stand beside S024's 97.56 / 96.19 / 27.14 %, with
# a same-tree control at the incumbent vector so the movement is attributed
# rather than explained.
#
# WHAT THIS IS. `adocs/data/S024_census_run.py run <engine>` over the same 400
# positions of `adocs/data/S024_census_positions.txt` -- one per game from
# `adocs/data/S219_aa_calibration.pgn`, `random.Random(24)` shuffle, each
# game's own midpoint ply -- at depth 10, Hash 16, `ucinewgame` between
# positions, driven through one persistent UCI process. The script is S024's
# unchanged; only the binary under it is new.
#
# THE BINARY. S222's fitted `src/search_params.hpp` -- the SPSA lane of
# 2026-09-14, `adocs/data/S222_spsa_trajectory.tsv` -- with S024's five
# throwaway counters patched back in. Built in a detached worktree at
# `bdd82cc` (S222 phase two's tree) with the fitted header copied in and the
# five counters added; `cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`, its own `build/`,
# the real tree's never touched, the worktree removed after the run. The
# instrumentation is not in the shipping engine and never was: an
# `info string cont_hist_census` line is not on the UCI surface
# `tests/test_uci_surface.cpp` guards. The exact diff is at the bottom of this
# file, so the run is reproducible without it having to exist in the tree.
#
# THE CONTROL, AND WHY IT IS HERE. Held against S024 alone the non-zero share
# fell eight points, and the obvious reading -- that the fitted scale writes a
# thinner table -- is an argument and not a measurement. So the same
# instrumented binary was rebuilt with `bdd82cc`'s own incumbent
# `search_params.hpp` and the same 400 positions re-run, which separates the
# vector from the tree: S109's pruning block and S091's capture rules landed
# between S024's census and this one, and the tree here is a third of the size
# (30.5 M nodes against 112.6 M over the same positions). Both summaries are
# below. **The fit is not what moved it**: at the incumbent vector on this tree
# the non-zero share is 18.94 %, at the fitted vector 19.15 %, so the fitted
# vector reads a non-zero entry slightly **more** often, by 0.21 points, and
# the whole of the eight-point fall belongs to the smaller tree.
#
# THE READING, beside S024's. Writes that have a previous move to index
# 96.62 % against 97.56 %; quiet `score_move()` evaluations that consult the
# continuation term 95.15 % against 96.19 %; of those, the share reading a
# non-zero entry 19.15 % against 27.14 %, of which none is the fit's doing per
# the control above. The first two are the same profile S024 measured and the
# small remainder is still exactly the root ply and the node after a null
# move; the per-position spread is 2.04 % to 38.88 %, median 17.12 %, so no
# handful of positions carries the average. What this census can say is what
# S024's said: the table is consulted on nearly every quiet score and returns
# a real number on a substantial share of those, so a verdict on the fitted
# vector is not a verdict on inert wiring. It is not a strength measurement
# and nothing here reads it as one (DEC-019); `adocs/data/S222_sprt.sh`
# decides the step.
#
# SUMMARY, FITTED VECTOR, as the script printed it:
#
#   positions: 400

#   wall time: 9.2 s

#   reads_nonzero: 11055397  of reads_with_prev: 57733854  share: 19.1489%
#   per-position reads_nonzero/reads_with_prev share: min 2.0426%  median 17.1180%  max 38.8845%
#
#   S024-CENSUS-DONE
#

# `src/search_params.hpp`, same 400 positions, same depth and hash:
